question: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle whose side is 10 cm. If height of this prism is 10sqrt{3} cm, then what is the total surface area of prism ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LSA = Perimeter of base × Height = (3 × 10) × 10√3 = 300√3 cm²

Base Area = (√3/4) × 10² = 25√3 cm²

TSA = LSA + 2 × Base Area = 300√3 + 2 × 25√3 = 350√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 350√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of equilateral base (a) = 10 cm

Height of prism (h) = 10√3 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Area of Base

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = Perimeter of base × height

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0d3e60a4fc526fd5bb7f9249e7b400105cc22da417077e75716359cf678713f.png] 

⇒ Area of base = (√3/4) × 10 × 10

⇒ Area of base = 25√3 cm²

⇒ Perimeter of base = 3 × 10 = 30 cm

⇒ LSA = 30 × 10√3 = 300√3 cm²

⇒ TSA = 300√3 + 2 × 25√3

⇒ TSA = 300√3 + 50√3

⇒ TSA = 350√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 350√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Prism

The volume of any right prism is calculated as Area of Base × Height.

Right Prism Definition

A prism in which the joining edges and faces are perpendicular to the base faces. All lateral faces are rectangles.

Area of Equilateral Triangle

For a triangle with side 'a', Area = (√3/4)a² and Height = (√3/2)a.</p
